pairs.why: A matches the real card's mild raised 3/4 view with a pool strip and tile ledge across the bottom, while B tilts the camera higher and closer, which exaggerates the platform's top and the ladder's convergence.
Both ropes have the same camera angle, the same near-top-down view and the same flat background, so viewpoint gives no reason to choose.
B puts the helmet on a flat floor with a clear horizon split like the real shoes card, while A's steep diagonal ledge and ball-like form read as a different, awkward camera.
B has a mild wall perspective and a gentle cornice angle like the real card, whereas A is wide-angle, with the left side swelling toward the camera and a steep ceiling line.
A looks down more steeply at the open lid and can tops, like the real card, while B's low, near-flat camera hides the top faces.
A shows slightly more top face and 3/4 tilt like the real calculator, but the two are very close.
A's high 3/4 camera shows the deck's top face and fills the frame like the real card, while B drops to a low, small, side-on view.
A crops the truss across the top edge and keeps the lamp large and central like the real card, while B floats a small whole truss in the frame, which weakens the layering.
